key_insight: Adding an AI teammate changes not just what teams decide, but how the human teammates talk to each other. The paper shows that artificial teammates can reshape human-human communication dynamics in small-group decision-making, with social costs that matter beyond task performance.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the gap in understanding how conversational AI teammates affect interpersonal communication inside human teams, especially in high-stakes collaborative decisions where trust, coordination, and shared reasoning matter.
method: Randomized controlled study comparing teams with an AI teammate vs. all-human teams
Small-team moral-dilemma decision task with two students per team plus AI in the treatment condition
Used Group Communication Analysis (GCA), team surveys, and lexical analysis of team discourse to measure sociocognitive communication patterns
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that evaluating AI teammates should include social and communication effects, not only accuracy or decision quality. Designing collaborative AI requires attention to team dynamics, shared voice, and whether the system disrupts or supports human-human coordination.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison diagram: all-human team vs. human+AI team
Flow chart of the experimental setup and decision task
Communication network or speech-bubble graphic showing interaction changes
Before/after chart of GCA or lexical metrics for team discourse
paper_title: The Social Cost of an AI Teammate: How an Artificial Teammate Reshapes Human-Human Communication in Small-Team Decision-Making
paper_authors: Nia Nixon, Jaeyoon Choi, Pedro Martins De Bastos, Mohammad Amin Samadi, Luise Mehner
